html:
The leader of the Khmer Rouge, who ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979. His regime caused the deaths of about 1.5 to 2 million people, close to a quarter of the population.

Born Saloth Sar, he studied in Paris around 1950 and joined the French Communist Party. Back home he rose to lead the small Cambodian communist party. In the chaos of the Vietnam War, with American bombing and a 1970 coup in Phnom Penh, his guerrillas grew strong.

They took Phnom Penh in April 1975 and at once carried out the emptying of the cities. Money, markets, schools and religion were abolished. People were made to farm in labour camps. Teachers, monks, officials, ethnic minorities and anyone thought disloyal were killed, many after torture in prisons such as S-21. Many more died of hunger and overwork. This was the Cambodian genocide.

Border attacks on Vietnam brought the Vietnamese invasion of late 1978, which drove him out. He fought on from the jungle and died in 1998, held by his own former comrades, without ever facing trial.
sum: The leader of the Khmer Rouge, who ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979. His regime caused the deaths of about 1.5 to 2 million people, close to a quarter of the population.
